relevance_note: Single case report of an ITGB2 compound-heterozygous LAD-I patient ("Two variants, namely c.533C>T, p.Pro178Leu and c.59-1G>A (NM_000211.5, NP_000202.3) in the ITGB2 gene, were identified"), plus two previously reported LAD-I transplant cases summarized in Table 1.
method_note: Hand-extracted; a Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans/fields. In scope: the index patient ('patient', rule 5; Table 1 column header 'Patient'), her father and mother (tested carriers via parental sequencing; the mother is also the HCT donor), and the two previously reported LAD-I patients summarized as columns of Table 1 ('Table 1 column 1' = column headed 'Khandewal et al. (21)'; 'Table 1 column 2' = 'Neven et al. (9)'). The paper spells the first author 'Khandewal' in Table 1 but 'Khandelwal' in the text. The donor fathers of the two literature cases are mentioned only as donors (not tested or affected) and get no rows. No ITGB2 variants are printed for the literature cases, so they have no variant rows. Table 1 'ND' is defined as 'not determined' and treated as not reported (Neven severity, CD34+/CD3+ doses). Table 1 'Other complications: No' for column 1 was not recorded as a feature (undefined feature). Table 1 'Outcome: Cured' was not taken as vital status for the literature cases. Possible contradiction: Table 1 gives 'Infectious complications pre-HCT: No' for the present patient, while the text reports recurrent omphalitis and repeated bacterial infections before HCT; both are recorded, and the omphalitis checklist item is kept observed because the table cell does not address omphalitis specifically (it likely refers to the immediate pre-HCT period, but the paper does not say). Umbilical cord separation 'occurred at 14 days of life' is not described by the authors as delayed, so 'delayed umbilical cord separation' is not reported. VOD/SOS is excluded for the two literature cases from the group statement 'none but the present case developed VOD/SOS' (the three Table 1 cases). Variant functional evidence is the patient's neutrophil CD18/CD11b/CD11c flow cytometry (person-level, both variants). Parents' zygosity and inheritance are not stated and left not reported; the father's protein notation comes from the patient's variant sentence. No stacked (' / ') cells in this paper.

span: Complete chimerism was achieved, and the patient was cured.
The patient has been well without complications except mild occasional skin GVHD

treatment_summary.value: prophylactic trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole; surgical excision of the urachal remnant at 10 months; HLA-haploidentical HCT with PBSCs from her mother after reduced-intensity conditioning (alemtuzumab, fludarabine, AUC-targeted busulfan); GVHD prophylaxis with PT-CY, tacrolimus and MMF
span: Prophylactic antimicrobial therapy with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole was initiated.
The patient underwent surgical excision of the urachal remnant when she was 10 months old.
Thus, the HLA-haploidentical mother was chosen as the donor for HCT.

Reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) consisted of alemtuzumab 0.8 mg/kg IV (0.16 mg/kg for 5 days; days –14 to –10), fludarabine 180 mg/m^2 IV (45 mg/m^2 for 4 days; days –9 to –6), and area under the curve (AUC)-targeted busulfan IV (65 mg*h/L; days –5 to –2)
GVHD prophylaxis included PT-CY 50 mg/kg IV on days +3 and +4, followed by tacrolimus continuous IV and oral mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) started on day +5.
